author_note: independent reference authored without access to the tool code
reference: Hand-built side-elevation scenarios for fall arrest (energy-absorbing lanyard and SRL), restraint and guardrail: anchor above / level with / below the D-ring, zero free fall, reserve and restraint boundaries at exactly zero and +/-0.01 m, obstacles under and away from the fall band, swing geometry at 0/30/60 deg and 3-4-5 triangles, user free-fall and rail-height limits, missing manufacturer data and invalid inputs, three OSHA Technical Manual worked examples, plus 28 seeded random cases. Numerical references are recomputed by ref.py with a coordinate construction of the lowest body position (pendulum settle below the anchor, then declared deployment and harness shift), not by re-summing the tool's component formula.
reference_citations: OSHA Technical Manual Section V Chapter 4 'Fall Protection in Construction', III.B (Total fall clearance distance; Examples 1b, 2, 4; swing fall) https://www.osha.gov/otm/section-5-construction-operations/chapter-4 (read 2026-09-16)
29 CFR 1926 Subpart M Appendix C, para (k) (tie-off at or above harness connection) and (m) (swing) https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1926/1926SubpartMAppC
ASSP 2013 PDC Session No. 617 'Fall Arrest Clearance Calculations Made Easy', pp. 7-14 https://aeasseincludes.assp.org/proceedings/2013/docs/617.pdf
Spec specs/05.md acceptance criteria; rigid-body plane geometry (ref.py)
tolerance: Numbers: relative 1e-9 (absolute 1e-9 m where the reference is 0). Every quantity is a closed-form sum/square root of the inputs with no iteration or discretisation, so any difference above floating-point rounding is a model difference, not numerical error. Categorical and boolean checks are exact.
